bull.b: Strong quarterly growth, rising backlog and a sizable commercial pipeline improve revenue visibility. If management converts advanced-stage opportunities, TOMI could build a larger customer base and establish a more durable operating scale.

Consumable solution sales complement equipment revenue and can create repeat purchasing as customers deploy SteraMist systems. This razor-and-blade structure may improve revenue continuity and customer retention across regulated facilities.

Additional regulatory labels, international approvals, intellectual property and marquee customer engagements broaden the addressable market. These developments support credibility in food safety, healthcare and life sciences, where validation can create durable adoption barriers.

bear.b: TOMI has not yet converted its gross profit into sustainable earnings, with multi-year operating and net losses. Continued losses constrain reinvestment and mean future growth must be funded before the business reaches durable profitability.

Rising leverage relative to equity increases financial risk and limits flexibility during expansion. A stressed capital base can raise dependence on external funding, increase dilution exposure and make execution more vulnerable to financing conditions.

Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that the current business model still consumes cash. This reduces the resources available for product development and commercialization while increasing reliance on equity lines or other capital.
